errors: No arithmetic errors found: all 49 sums D + v = D' check to 0.001", and every reciprocal pair satisfies (D'_ji − 180°) − D'_ij = t_ij exactly with t_ji = −t_ij.

Gauss himself flags an input error: Bremen→Garlste was used as 165°11'50.407" instead of 49.407" (1" too large). He propagates its effect on the orientation unknowns rather than redoing the adjustment.

The parenthetical station quantities (+0.063 etc.) do not equal the mean of the listed station corrections. For Wilsede the mean is −0.046, not +0.063. Their exact definition (orientation unknowns relative to some provisional orientation) cannot be verified from this page alone.

results.what: Least-squares adjustment of a triangulation network of oriented directions, with station orientation unknowns and reciprocal-direction (angle) conditions only; side conditions are postponed to a second stage.
results.modern_name: Least-squares network adjustment by directions (combined station/orientation unknowns and condition equations), stepwise adjustment
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss (Hannover triangulation 1821–25; Supplementum theoriae combinationis 1826/28)

results.what: Reduction terms t_ij linking forward and back directions in Gauss's projection; reciprocal pairs differ by exactly ±t_ij.
results.modern_name: Arc-to-chord (t−T) reduction / meridian convergence in Gauss conformal (Gauss–Krüger) coordinates
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss (conformal projection for the Hannover survey; later Schreiber, Krüger)

results.what: Propagation of a 1" correction of one observation (Bremen→Garlste) to all orientation unknowns via influence coefficients, without re-solving the system.
results.modern_name: Sensitivity analysis / column of inverse normal matrix (influence of a single observation update)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (practice of correcting adjusted solutions); generally standard in least squares

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine worked table from Gauss's well-documented Hannover triangulation, applying his own least-squares direction adjustment. The influence-coefficient correction is a nice practical detail but is in line with known Gauss geodetic practice.
transcription_corrections: Column (iv) values are in thousandths of an arcsecond (e.g. −1252 = −1.252"); the machine transcription leaves units implicit.
Brelit and Garlste carry no station number in the manuscript, consistent with their absence from the side conditions on the next page.
